criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear mission purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), identified users (marine/conservation scientists), strong need justification with statistics and four cited sources. However, no explicit mission objectives/requirements list (orbit, resolution, coverage targets), keeping it at the lower end of Accomplished.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Week-by-week Gantt chart with colour-coded completion status, deadlines, and detailed task narratives tied to the mission (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, end of life). Information sources listed. Lacks explicit contingency/variation provisions, so lower end of Accomplished.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Evidence of work: literature reading, completed mission concept, and four STK tutorials. However, no preliminary technical results (no orbit calculations, payload sizing, or simulation outputs) are presented or interpreted, so progress is real but modest.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical structure, clear headings, good writing quality, footnoted citations matching listed URLs, well-explained Gantt chart. Weaknesses: raw URLs instead of formatted references, 'Useful Links' not a formal reference list, and Image 1 lacks a numbered figure caption — lower end of Accomplished.

evidence.quote: Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution leading to the bleaching of coral reefs.¹
Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines.

technical_issues.issue: No quantitative mission requirements (orbit altitude, revisit time, spatial/spectral resolution, payload definition) despite proposing imaging for bleaching detection.
No preliminary technical results shown; STK tutorial completion is asserted but not evidenced with outputs or interpretation.
References are raw URLs with footnote superscripts rather than a properly formatted, cited reference list.
Gantt chart lacks a figure number/caption.

overall: A well-written, clearly structured preliminary report with a compelling GBR monitoring mission concept, a detailed Gantt-chart plan, and listed sources. Main gaps: no explicit mission requirements, no preliminary technical results beyond tutorials, and informal referencing.

feedback.summary: A well-written, clearly structured report with a compelling Great Barrier Reef bleaching-monitoring concept, a detailed week-by-week Gantt chart, and listed sources. To strengthen the submission, add explicit quantitative mission requirements, present preliminary technical results from your STK work, and convert your footnoted URLs into a properly formatted reference list.
next_steps: Define quantitative mission requirements (orbit altitude, revisit time, spatial/spectral resolution, payload definition) and link each to user needs.
Include preliminary technical outputs from STK (e.g., orbit plots, coverage/access results) with brief interpretation, rather than only asserting tutorial completion.
Add contingency provisions to your plan (e.g., what to do if STK simulations or data access fall behind) and explain why the plan is sequenced this way.
Replace raw-URL footnotes with a formatted reference list (e.g., IEEE style) and give Image 1 a numbered figure caption.

criteria.C1: Your mission concept is clear and well justified: the GBR bleaching-monitoring purpose, users (marine and conservation scientists), and need are supported with statistics and four cited sources. To move higher within Accomplished, add an explicit objectives/requirements list — target orbit, revisit time, spatial/spectral resolution, and payload definition — each tied to user needs and literature.
criteria.C2: Your week-by-week Gantt chart with colour-coded status, deadlines, and task narratives tied to the mission (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, end of life) is a strong plan, and your information sources are listed. To reach the top of the rubric, add explicit contingency/variation provisions and justify why the plan is sequenced this way in the context of the mission.
criteria.C3: You have done real work — literature reading, the mission concept, and STK tutorials 1–4 — but no preliminary technical results are presented. To reach Accomplished, include actual outputs (orbit calculations, COEs/AOEs, coverage simulations, or payload sizing) with brief description and interpretation to show you are clearly on track.
criteria.C4: Your report is logically structured, easy to read, and the Gantt chart is well explained. To strengthen presentation, replace raw-URL footnotes with a properly formatted reference list cited consistently in text, and add a numbered caption to Image 1 so figures are formally labelled.
